key_insight: As training progressed, ResNet50 and ConvNeXt-Tiny produced more faithful, less sensitive explanations, while VGG16 yielded simpler but less faithful and correct explanations.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform explainability evaluation for medical imaging AI, but the study used ImageNet rather than clinical data.
method: Trained VGG16, ResNet50, and ConvNeXt-Tiny on 10 ImageNet-1K subsets with 80 classes each.
Applied Grad-CAM and CRAFT at 10 checkpoints per model.
Evaluated Faithfulness, Correctness, Sensitivity, and Simplicity.
evidence_signal: The evaluation spanned 30 trained models and 300 model checkpoints, comparing two explanation methods across four evaluation categories.
watch_item: Improved explanation metrics do not establish clinical reliability; validation on medical images and clinically meaningful tasks remains necessary.
paper_title: How a Model's Architecture and Performance Influences Explainability: A Study of Grad-CAM and CRAFT in CNN-Based Image Classification
